doc.title: Carl Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, Georgia, January 4, 2013

title: What young players like, and the jazz students who never play jazz
summary: Allen says young players follow Glasper, Iyer and Loueke, and worries that jazz majors graduate without having played Basie, Monk or Duke; he programs traditional music at Juilliard.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Who would the 17- and 18-year-olds be passionate about, in your experience?
Robert Glasper. A lot of the young kids are really into Glasper. Vijay Iyer. Lionel Loueke.
Wow. I guess I would have guessed, well it probably speaks to my age, but maybe even like the Michael Brecker generation.

Oh. A lot of those kids don’t even know who he was. It’s interesting. You know we had an experience at Juilliard recently, something that happened that really hurt me. We had did a concert. One of the things that I try to do in our program, from a programming perspective, is, you know I look at music that I think the students should know. And I try

to deal with something from a traditional perspective, something a little bit more modern, you know, because I often think about my experiences when I would visit colleges and universities to do master classes and concerts, and I’m dealing with jazz majors, and they don’t have any jazz in their book. And I ask the instructors, I say, “Well why is it you have all this pop/hip hop stuff in their book?”
